analysis: Reviewed the base text of docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (lines 448-1236) against the patch excerpt. The change is documentation only: it bumps the date (line 3), adds a paragraph at about lines 559-574 describing a floor-aware `resliceGrants` for KV re-slicing (floors honored when the sum fits the budget, otherwise the proportional split stands and `resliceMeetsServiceabilityFloor` refuses), and edits the invariants near lines 850-853. No executable code, keys, wire contracts, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-at-rest behavior is changed. The prose describes availability and memory-admission behavior (KV slot grants, TB-007; T-029-style resource concerns). It states that a newcomer's floor is checked only at engine assembly and can fail with `no_kv_headroom`. That fails closed (a refused load) and does not weaken a confidentiality or integrity boundary. The T-041 prefix-cache material (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, account scoping) is not touched by the visible diff, and the base text does not contradict it. The patch excerpt is truncated (`patch_excerpt_complete` is false), so I could not see the remaining edits near lines 850-867. The changed ranges show only the invariant and failure-mode area plus one code-map line. The source implementation (`EngineV2KVSizing`, `ProviderLoop`, `EngineV2Bridge`) is not supplied, so I cannot confirm that the doc matches the code. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a security regression. No threat-model updates are needed from this change.
